it enters model context; obfuscation-resistant; credential files quarantined on path alone
# dsh-read-guard
> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!

Deterministic prompt-injection interception for
DeepSeek Harness (dsh).

**Vendors harden only their own agents at runtime. This plugin is the runtime.**
It hooks dsh's `too

ls/post-execute` waterfall: every result the watched tools
return — file reads, repo searches, web f

etches — is scanned by the
repo-inject-guard rule
engine **at the moment it would enter model contex

t**, then quarantined,
blocked, or passed. Zero LLM calls in the trust path.
The name states the thesis: it guards what the agent *reads*.
## Why

Repo poisoning and web-content injection enter through what the agent *reads*,
not what the user typ

es. Scanning files at commit time (CI) is too late for a
live session; scanning after the fact is an

autopsy. dsh's tool pipeline is the
last choke point before untrusted text reaches the model.
## Competitive landscape (checked 2026-10-12)

The injection-defense lane is a long tail without a winner (~15 plugins, none
above 85★). The ones t
hat matter, honestly:
| Plugin | Architecture | What we do differently |
| dsh-secure-audit (85★) | Scanning is a **model-callable tool** — the model must volunteer to call

it | We intercept in the tools/post-execute waterfall; the model cannot bypass the scan. |
| dsh-def
end (23★) | Same three interception points, allow/ask/block, Aho-Corasick literal patterns | Our eng
ine is context-scoped (rules fire per trust level / surface, with corroboration requirements) rather
than literal pattern lists; `wrap` mode keeps content available while taint-marked (theirs is allow

/ask/block only); scan cap 200k full-text vs their 10k head-only |
| dsh-injection-guard (2★) | Acti
on-side taint tracking (blocks sensitive tool calls after untrusted context) | Complementary, not co
mpeting: they gate downstream actions, we sanitize upstream content. (We renamed from `dsh-inject-gu
ard` to avoid confusion with them.) |

We are not first. The bet is that a precision-first engine with upstream tests
(the rule engine live

s in repo-inject-guard with its own CI and fixture suite)
plus enforcement-not-advice architecture o
utlasts weekend pattern lists.
## Modes
| mode | high-severity finding | weak (medium/low) finding |

| `observe` | logged | logged |
| `wrap` (default) | result is taint-marked: original content stays
model-visible inside quarantine markers with an explicit "this is data, not instructions" header | l

ogged only — precision first, we never mangle legitimate content over weak signals |
| `block` | res
ult never reaches the model; the model gets corrective feedback instead | logged only |

Detection rules (vendored engine): instruction-override attempts, system-prompt
extraction, credenti

al/environment exfiltration, hidden Unicode, agent
directives, rules-file backdoor phrasing, resourc

e lures. Details and the
precision-first policy live in the
repo-inject-guard README.

## Compatibility
- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile

via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/

24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fr
esh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-read-guard` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-read-guard] active
: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-read-guard` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Load from source into a local dsh checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The detection engine is vendored from the sibling `repo-inject-guard`
checkout (`npm run sync`; CI r

uns `sync --check`). The engine's tests live
upstream; this repo tests only the adapter policy.
## Roadmap

- `agent/pre-step` scanning for pasted user content (deliberately out of v0:
users are allowed to gi

ve instructions)
- MCP-server tool surfaces as a preset trust class
- Per-agent scoped policies (dsh

scopes allow agent-local listeners)
- A report tool card (`presentResult`) surfacing session detect

ow agent-local listeners)
- A report tool card (`presentResult`) surfacing session detection history
## Kill criteria

Honest ones, per house convention: if dsh ships a first-party content-safety
guard covering tool-res

ult injection, or the `tools/post-execute` contract
changes in a way that breaks content replacement

, this plugin freezes at its
last working version and the README records the postmortem. The engine

moves
to whatever runtime needs it next.
## Known limitations
Stated plainly, so you can decide whether this guard fits your threat model:
- **Scan scope is config-driven.** Only the tools listed in `readTools` / `fetchTools` are watched (
default: read/grep/glob + web_fetch/web_search). MCP tools, shell output, and other content channels

are not scanned unless you add them.
- **Text blocks only.** Non-text content blocks (images, etc.)

pass through untouched; per-result scanning stops at `maxScanChars` (default 200,000).
- **Wrap mod
e keeps the original text in context**, explicitly marked untrusted — it does not remove it. High-se

verity findings mutate the result; medium/low are report-only.
- **One channel of many.** Blocking o
ne tool result does not prove the model cannot receive the same content through another path.
